newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees pressure from growing China.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees pressure from growing China.

text.p: China's rapid growth will place political and military pressure on east Asia and the region still needs the stablising presence of the United States, Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Monday.

"These (next 10-15) years will be crucial, because they may turn out to be the last years of the post-Cold war area, the last years of the superiority which America and its allies enjoy," he said in his last state-of-nation address to Congress.
"This period of stability underwritten by America's economic and military strength would not last forever. The future simply holds too many uncertainties," he said.
Ramos pointed to doubts over China's intentions in the South China Sea, where Manila and Beijing have been squabbling over small reefs and islands whih both claim.
There were questions too over how Russia would emerge as a power, what will happen on the Korean peninsula and how Japan will respond to the challenge of ensuring peace in the region.
"China's rapidly expanding economy will unavoidably press politically and militarily in Asia...it is unreasonable for anyone to think that outsiders can prevent (it becoming a great power)."
Ramos said southeast Asian countries agreed that the best approach to China was to draw it into their network of economic and diplomatic collaboration.
But he reiterated that in this time of uncertainty the United States should stay in Asia-Pacific as a "force for stabilising the regional power balance."
The Philippines, host to two huge U.S. military bases until 1991, also needed to boost its own defences and develop a credible air and naval capability, he added.
